roles.name: --border
roles.purpose: frames and lines: a frame on a resting container and the splits between its sections, a line on controls and between rows

roles.name: --card
roles.purpose: a resting container that holds content, framed by a frame border

roles.name: --gap-default
roles.purpose: field to field, block to block, card to card
roles.why: A back office is compact by definition: its gaps, its field and row sizes, its text sizes and weights and its page edge are part of what it is.

roles.name: --gap-related
roles.purpose: buttons in a row, options in a group
roles.why: A back office is compact by definition: its gaps, its field and row sizes, its text sizes and weights and its page edge are part of what it is.

roles.why: A back office is compact by definition: its gaps, its field and row sizes, its text sizes and weights and its page edge are part of what it is.

roles.name: --line-height-heading
roles.purpose: card, section and surface headings, and the text typed into a field
roles.why: A back office is compact by definition: its gaps, its field and row sizes, its text sizes and weights and its page edge are part of what it is.

roles.name: --page-edge
roles.purpose: the page's edge, narrower on a phone than from a tablet up
roles.why: A back office is compact by definition: its gaps, its field and row sizes, its text sizes and weights and its page edge are part of what it is.

roles.name: --primary-ink
roles.purpose: the brand colour as text or a glyph on a surface — a link, a record's mark — readable in both themes where the brand fill itself is not

roles.name: --radius-control
roles.purpose: a thing that IS content: a button, a field, a nav item

roles.name: --step-16
roles.why: A back office is compact by definition: its gaps, its field and row sizes, its text sizes and weights and its page edge are part of what it is.

roles.name: --weight-body
roles.why: A back office is compact by definition: its gaps, its field and row sizes, its text sizes and weights and its page edge are part of what it is.

roles.name: --weight-emphasis
roles.purpose: a column heading, a field error, a nav group, the status strip, a table footer
roles.why: A back office is compact by definition: its gaps, its field and row sizes, its text sizes and weights and its page edge are part of what it is.

roles.name: --weight-heading
roles.purpose: a card or section heading, a readout caption, a figure, initials
roles.why: A back office is compact by definition: its gaps, its field and row sizes, its text sizes and weights and its page edge are part of what it is.

roles.name: border-frame
roles.purpose: The two line roles — every border is one of them, by its job. A frame is a container's edge and the splits and header bands between its sections. A line is a control's edge, an overlay's edge, and the rules between rows or items.

roles.name: scroll-region
roles.purpose: A region that scrolls vertically inside its own box, with the bar hidden. `position: relative` is load-bearing: without it an `sr-only` label inside the region is positioned against the page and gives the whole screen a scrollbar. Use this — never a bare `overflow-y-auto`.

roles.name: type-body
roles.purpose: prose — descriptions, list text, dialog text
roles.value: font-size: var(--step-14); font-weight: var(--weight-body); line-height: var(--line-height-body)
roles.why: A back office is compact by definition: its gaps, its field and row sizes, its text sizes and weights and its page edge are part of what it is.

roles.name: type-surface-heading
roles.purpose: names a section inside an overlay surface — a step under the dialog's title, a step over its text
roles.value: font-size: var(--step-16); font-weight: var(--weight-heading); line-height: var(--line-height-heading)
roles.why: A back office is compact by definition: its gaps, its field and row sizes, its text sizes and weights and its page edge are part of what it is.
